questions.q: What two events did the External RDP Allow + Entra Sign-In Correlation rule match at 3 a.m.?
options: Two unrelated firewall allow events
A firewall allow from 203.0.114.77 to the admin jump host on RDP, and an Entra sign-in for n.pettit@hartwellru.com from that same address five minutes later
Two sign-ins from two different Linux servers
A Syslog entry and a Windows Security Event
questions.explain: The rule's join found a firewall RDP allow and an Entra sign-in from the same source address, inside its 15-minute window.

questions.q: Which firewall rule allowed the connection from 203.0.114.77 to reach the admin jump host?
options: A brand-new rule written that same night
TEMP-MERIDIAN-RDP, the rule set up in Lesson 4
The default-deny rule
A rule specific to n.pettit's account
questions.explain: The connection was allowed through TEMP-MERIDIAN-RDP, the rule created during the Lesson 4 vendor-access setup.

questions.q: Why did the n.pettit sign-in need only a valid password, with no MFA challenge?
options: MFA was broken tenant-wide
n.pettit's account isn't in the CA-Pilot-SOC-IT group yet, so the Conditional Access pilot policy doesn't apply to it
Owen Mercer disabled MFA for all help-desk accounts
The sign-in came from a compliant device, which exempts it from MFA
questions.explain: The Conditional Access pilot is scoped only to CA-Pilot-SOC-IT; n.pettit's account isn't in that group, so only a password was required.

questions.q: What did Mara's Triage checks conclude about this alert?
options: It's clearly routine vendor activity -- closed as benign
Every check (unusual hour, unrecognized address, out-of-pilot account, successful sign-in) pointed toward a real concern, so she escalated past Triage into Scope
It's a false positive caused by a misconfigured rule query
It can't be triaged without more log sources
questions.explain: The account's unusual hour, the unrecognized source address, the pilot-group gap, and the successful sign-in all pointed toward a genuine concern.

questions.q: What question does Triage leave unanswered at the end of this lesson?
options: Nothing -- the investigation is fully resolved
How 203.0.114.77, an address with no business reaching the admin port, was allowed through the firewall in the first place
Whether n.pettit's password was strong enough
Whether the Conditional Access pilot group should be renamed
questions.explain: Triage confirmed the symptom was real but didn't yet explain the underlying cause -- why the firewall allowed that address through at all.
